shots.prompt: Create ONE horizontal widescreen 16:9 photorealistic cinematic film still for the Tokyo noir drama Nobody's Witness: the epilogue, inside Kaneko's tiny noodle bar under a brick railway arch at night. Compose a slightly closer shot on that shelf, seen at a three-quarter angle from the counter side: a small old dusty CRT television, sound off, on the wooden shelf above the dark blue noren curtain. On its small screen, the evening news: the composed Japanese politician KUROSE — matching the exact face, age, swept-back silver hair and heavy-lidded calm of the man in the second reference — in a dark navy suit and tie, walking toward a building entrance between two suited lawyers, press photographers' flashbulbs flaring white around him, cool grey daylight behind them on the screen. Foreground and lower edge stay soft: the warm bare bulb, the brick arch, drifting steam, and behind them Kaneko at the counter and a dark-coated man on a stool with an empty space beside him. Warm tungsten light on the set's dusty plastic casing against the cold grey-blue light of its own screen, muted midnight-teal palette, restrained 35mm film grain, true 16:9 landscape frame with comfortable headroom. The screen's lower third is only a plain soft bar with no lettering; no captions, subtitles, chyrons, readable or invented text, logos or watermarks anywhere.
